items.title: Triplicated XML rendering pattern — tools, skills, roster
items.description: The XML-fragment builder pattern is implemented independently three times: ToolRegistry.format_for_prompt() (tool_registry.py:258-277), SkillRegistry.format_for_prompt() (skill_registry.py:85-91), and MessagingModule._build_roster() (messaging/__init__.py:231-254). Each rolls its own lines-list accumulation, xml_escape calls, and tag construction. Any change to the serialization contract (e.g., switching to JSON, adding a wrapper envelope, adding a version attribute) must be applied in three unrelated places. Per the project standard, three instances of a pattern is the extraction threshold.

items.title: agent.py reaches into ToolRegistry._prompt_cache private field
items.description: _setup_tool_prompt_injection() (agent.py:476) reads tool_registry._prompt_cache directly to determine whether the cache was cold before calling format_for_prompt(), so it can conditionally emit a telemetry audit event. This breaks encapsulation: agent.py is coupled to the internal caching implementation of ToolRegistry. If the cache strategy changes (e.g., keyed cache, weak-ref cache, moved into a property) agent.py must change in lockstep and mypy --strict will not catch the breakage because _prompt_cache is typed str | None, not a Protocol boundary. The fix is to expose a public cache_is_warm: bool property or return a CatalogResult dataclass with a rebuilt: bool field from format_for_prompt().

items.title: _build_roster made async as SDD deviation — inconsistent with sync format_for_prompt pattern
items.description: The SDD for SPEC-013 specified _build_roster as a synchronous method matching the pattern of ToolRegistry.format_for_prompt() and SkillRegistry.format_for_prompt(). It was made async during implementation because it calls self._registry.list_entities() which is async (messaging/__init__.py:210, 225). This is architecturally correct given the async registry, but it creates an asymmetry: two of the three XML-building methods are sync, one is async. _on_assemble_prompt (line 266) must await _build_roster() while the tool/skill injection handlers call format_for_prompt() synchronously inside an otherwise-async closure. This asymmetry will confuse contributors and complicates any future shared XmlPromptBuilder abstraction. The deviation should be formally recorded in an ADR or the SDD updated to reflect the async contract.

items.title: _DEFAULT_PREAMBLE hardcoded module-level string in tool_registry.py
items.description: The fallback preamble text ('You have the following tools available. Use them as needed to accomplish your tasks.') is a bare module-level constant at tool_registry.py:31-34. It is not surfaced in config.py schema documentation, not validated, and carries no reference to where it can be overridden. This is a configuration-as-code anti-pattern for a federal-grade system: preamble text is prompt content that may need classification-aware tuning or environment-specific wording without a code change. It should be defined in the Pydantic ToolsConfig as the field default (with Field(default=..., description='...')), making it self-documenting and overridable at the config layer.

items.title: roster_ttl_seconds default of 60.0s is undocumented magic number
items.description: MessagingConfig.roster_ttl_seconds defaults to 60.0 (messaging/config.py:49) with no inline rationale. The number is tested (test_config.py:46-54) but neither the config schema nor the field docstring explains why 60 seconds was chosen, what the failure mode is if it is set too low (stale roster during rapid agent join/leave) or too high (agents invisible to teammates for too long). In a multi-agent federal system, roster freshness is a trust and correctness concern. The field needs a Field(default=60.0, description='...', gt=0) with inline rationale and the test should assert behavior at boundary values, not just the default.

items.title: test_shutdown_invalidates_cache is a hollow test — does not actually verify behavior
items.description: test_tool_registry.py:518-525 is named test_shutdown_invalidates_cache and asserts reg.format_for_prompt() != '' before shutdown, then leaves a comment saying 'We test the register/format cycle — shutdown clears _tools dict' without calling shutdown() or asserting the post-shutdown state. The test name promises one behavior and the body verifies a weaker, different behavior. Any regression in the shutdown cache-invalidation path would not be caught. The test should call await reg.shutdown() and then assert reg.format_for_prompt() == '' after.

items.title: No integration test covering _setup_tool_prompt_injection end-to-end
items.description: _setup_tool_prompt_injection() (agent.py:463-491) is the critical wiring point that subscribes to agent:assemble_prompt and injects the tool catalog into the sections dict. The only test that touches this code path (test_agent.py:594-604) tests _setup_skill_prompt_injection (not tool) and only verifies the None-bus early-return guard — it does not subscribe a real bus, emit agent:assemble_prompt, and assert that sections['tools'] is populated with the correct XML. The was_cached conditional audit event path (agent.py:480-484) has zero test coverage. This is a core correctness guarantee for SPEC-013 that is untested at the integration seam.

items.title: Core LOC budget exceeded — 3,723 lines against 3,500 limit
items.description: The project constitution (CLAUDE.md) sets a hard ceiling of 3,500 LOC for packages/arcagent/src/arcagent/core/. The current count is 3,723 lines across 14 files, a 6.4% overage. The two largest contributors are agent.py (553 LOC) and extensions.py (551 LOC), both of which now exceed the individual file size where scrolling is required (violating the readability standard). SPEC-013 added format_for_prompt(), the cache, and the two _setup_*_prompt_injection methods, contributing approximately 80 net lines. The budget must be restored before the next feature lands in core. Candidate extractions: the XML rendering logic (see TD-001, ~30 LOC) and the prompt injection setup methods (~60 LOC) into a PromptAssembler coordinator that lives in core/ but is isolated from agent.py.
